stories.headline: Figure reports 56 percent success for humanoid in 30 unseen homes
stories.standfirst: The company rented the Bay Area properties for the test, and says an identical model trained without its human-video dataset managed 9 percent.
body: Figure released Helix 2.5 on Wednesday and said the model completed 56 percent of household tasks across 30 Bay Area homes it had not trained on. The company said it rented the properties for the evaluation. The robots tidied living rooms, folded towels and made beds.

The comparison Figure draws is with itself. An identical model trained without Index, its dataset of first-person human video, completed 9 percent of the same trials. Figure gives the task breakdown as 67 percent for making beds, 62 percent for folding towels and 40 percent for tidying toys away.

The term zero-shot is narrower than it may appear. Figure says the robot had not seen the homes or the objects, but it specified the three tasks using fine-tuning data gathered elsewhere. The company gave no partial credit and counted every safety intervention as a failure, which makes 56 percent a strict measure rather than a flattering one.

Tony Zhao of Sunday Robotics, quoted by Humanoids Daily, said the system is failing half the time, and that useful work needs reliability as well as generalisation. Figure designed and scored the evaluation itself. No independent replication has appeared.
